reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a paid trading sniper bot as a way to buy tokens faster and potentially earn substantially more, while directing viewers to purchase it and contact the seller. The demonstrated setup instructs users to place a wallet private key into the bot, creating a direct account-control risk beyond an ordinary trading tutorial. The video also claims the bot can allow users to do "x2 or x3 more" than manual trading, encouraging participation through an easy-profit representation.

citations.quote: Today I will present you my new sniper bot
After wallet address you go on your Metamask here you copy the public address here you put and the private key
I have put the link in description of this bot for those who are interested
It will allow to do x2 or x3 more than if you got in manually
go to shopie.gg and buy something now with paypal

opening.argument: The presenter expressly separates the tool from investment responsibility: “I am not responsible for all your investments.” He also warns users, “You must not share this to others,” and states, “There is no system that will try to send your private key.” Those are direct risk and security cautions, not the language of a guaranteed-return solicitation. The presentation leaves the financial decision to the viewer and describes a configurable tool whose results depend on the user’s own trading choices.

citations.quote: I am not responsible for all your investments
You must not share this to others
There is no system that will try to send your private key

rebuttal.rebuttal: The purchase link and the “x2 or x3” comparison establish promotion, but not deception or a promised outcome. The statement is framed as a comparison with manual entry, while the same speaker expressly disclaims responsibility for investments. The private-key instruction is accompanied by a warning not to share it and a denial that the system sends it.

citations.quote: It will allow to do x2 or x3 more than if you got in manually
I am not responsible for all your investments
You must not share this to others

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the conduct being promoted. The presenter still instructs viewers to place a private key into the configuration and directs them to purchase the bot. The warning not to share the key concedes that the bot receives it; saying the system will not send it elsewhere is only an unsupported assurance, not independent protection.

citations.quote: After wallet address you go on your Metamask here you copy the public address here you put and the private key
I have put the link in description of this bot for those who are interested
There is no system that will try to send your private key

opening.argument: The primary activity is operational instruction and demonstration. The speaker explains what a sniper bot is, walks through configuration, and presents the PancakeSwap workflow rather than merely asserting that viewers will profit. He explicitly introduces the material as an explanation and says the guide remains available for people who need configuration help. The displayed application and transaction workflow therefore support treating this as a technology tutorial demonstrating user-controlled trading settings, not proof of a fraudulent scheme.

citations.quote: Today I will present you my new sniper bot
The PANCAKE SWAP GUIDE is always available
I will first explain it to you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of a tutorial does not turn its subject into a scam. Showing configuration fields, purchase execution, and sell controls is consistent with demonstrating software operation. The reference argument identifies a risk associated with the tool, but it does not establish that the walkthrough fabricated results, concealed a failure, or guaranteed profit.

citations.quote: Liquidity detected, it has directly purchased
This means that the sell will start and it will sell as soon as it reaches your target
there is still the pancake swap guide for those who need it for the configuration

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not a detached lesson about software. The speaker says the bot is available to interested viewers, supplies a purchase route, and ends by directing them to buy. The demonstration is the sales pitch: it presents automated buying and selling, then claims the tool can produce substantially more than manual trading. Operational detail does not erase that solicitation.

citations.quote: I have put the link in description of this bot for those who are interested
go to shopie.gg and buy something now with paypal
It will allow to do x2 or x3 more than if you got in manually

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows ordinary commerce for a software product. The supplied product page identifies a “SNIPER BOT (Binance Smart Chain)” and displays a $200.00 purchase option, while the description lists functions such as take profit, stop loss, and force sell. A price and a purchase button establish a retail transaction, not a deposit scheme, downline, or guaranteed return. The materials do not establish that the seller takes custody of funds, promises reimbursement, or receives referral income.

citations.quote: Several available functions such as TP (Take Profit) The SL (Stop Loss) or the FS (Force Sell)
go to shopie.gg and buy something now with paypal

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from the product’s crypto setting and its access requirements, but the evidence also supports a conventional sale of a software tool. The $200 page shows a purchase option, not a transfer of trading capital or a return guarantee. The claimed “x2 or x3” benefit is promotional language, yet no fixed result or repayment promise is stated.

citations.quote: It will allow to do x2 or x3 more than if you got in manually
Do not hesitate to place the order on the site

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The retail framing overlooks the unusually consequential access instruction: users are told to enter an existing wallet’s private key into the bot, while the bot is configured to trade funded balances. The product page and payment route confirm solicitation; they do not validate the software. A fixed guarantee is unnecessary where the combination of paid promotion, private-key handling, and easy-profit claims creates the risk.
